bull_bear.body: Priorities: 1) fund committed capex (INR220Cr), 2) retain dry powder (INR2,437M net cash) for inorganic acquisitions, 3) dividend payout of 35% of face value (INR3.5/share); no debt used, debt-free balance sheet maintained
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global supply chain disruptions; geopolitical volatility affecting export markets; delay in BOE display product qualification; slower-than-expected ramp-up of new WPI programs; currency fluctuations impacting export profitability
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on FY27; emphasized disciplined execution, margin expansion, and strategic patience in export and inorganic growth; reiterated 26-year track record of outperformance; tone was assertive on technology leadership and operational excellence
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Export intensity is understated in consolidated figures — SJS standalone export contribution is significantly higher than reported due to SDPL/WPI being domestic-focused; BOE partnership is not just about displays but about vertical integration of aesthetic + electronic functions, positioning SJS as a holistic cabin experience partner
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free on long-term debt across FY25, FY26 and Q1FY27 (all zero), with total debt of only Rs 93 Mn at Q1FY27 against cash and cash equivalents of Rs 3,381 Mn, giving net cash of Rs 3,287.7 Mn as on 30th June 2026.
- ICRA upgraded SJS long term funds rating to AA- (Positive) from AA- (Stable); strong cash flow generation is stated as supporting expansion initiatives.
- ROCE progression of 25% (FY25), 36% (FY26), 37% (Q1FY27) and ROE of 17%, 20%, 20%; deck text states ROE and ROCE improved to 20.3% and 37.2%.
- FCFF of Rs 1,233 Mn (FY25), Rs 1,427 Mn (FY26) and Rs 838 Mn (Q1FY27); total equity of Rs 9,583 Mn at Q1FY27.
- The deck makes no mention of dividend, buyback or a stated payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: 2-wheeler: 38.3% of FY26 revenue, grew 4x industry; passenger vehicle: 41.7% of FY26 revenue, grew 3x industry; consumer & others: 20% of FY26 revenue, rationalized low-margin products, new high-margin programs ramping up
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Operates in the high value-add aesthetics market across multiple consumer-oriented end industries, focused on premium aesthetic products and innovative designs, with in-house design and R&D capabilities.
- Describes itself as partner, co-creator and supplier of choice to several leading OEMs in the automotive and consumer durables industry; deck's timeline notes that on listing in Nov-21 SJS 'is the only listed company in India in this space'.
- Claims outperformance of industry growth for the 27th consecutive quarter; Q1FY27 automotive growth of 32.4% YoY versus 21.7% YoY for the automotive (2W+PV) industry production volumes, described as 1.5x growth v/s industry.
- SJS in-house R&D centre achieved recognition by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order book] Current order book to be executed in FY27 is over 88% of FY27 forecasted revenue; SJS expects to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5-2x.
- [Exceptional item] Reported PAT includes a Rs 241.7 Mn exceptional gain — a one-time post-tax gain on sale of the Bangalore old facility, which was not in use since 2019.
- [Ownership] Aug'23 saw a stake sale of ~30% by PE promoter Everstone Capital, which had acquired a majority stake in 2015 with Serigraph exiting.
- [Governance] Board is chaired by a Non-Executive Chairman & Independent Director; the ESG annexure reports 57.14% independent board of directors and 16.7% founder board members.
- [Outlook wording] The FY27 outlook bullet reads 'Continue to maintain robust margin profile of business for FY26' — the deck refers to FY26 in an FY27 outlook slide.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 30.3% due to premium product mix (24% of revenue from new-gen products), higher export contribution (60.5% YoY growth), operational efficiencies, and back-to-back cost pass-throughs on chrome plating inputs; polymer cost inflation mitigated by annual product refresh pricing
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: outperform industry by 1.5x–2x in FY27; margin: target 27–28% long-term; order inflow: strong pipeline across global OEMs; capex/commissioning: INR145Cr total capex planned over FY26–FY28 (INR80Cr done in FY26), including INR45Cr Bangalore expansion (20% capacity), INR100Cr SDPL chrome greenfield (commissioning complete), and display facility in Hosur (equipment ordered, production expected end-FY27/early-FY28)
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: BOE Varitronix optical display partnership (cover glass, TFT bonding) to unlock $4B global market; export expansion into Germany, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea; inorganic acquisitions in NA, SEA, India targeting margin-accretive players
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SJS delivered record Q4FY26 revenue and PAT driven by 41% YoY automotive segment growth and 75% export surge, with EBITDA margin expanding to 30.3% due to premiumization and operational efficiency; the strategic BOE Varitronix partnership for optical display systems and aggressive capacity expansion position the company to outperform industry growth by 1.5x–2x in FY27, leveraging its 24% revenue from new-gen products.

open.item: SJS aims to increase the share of exports to 14%-15% of total revenue by FY28, driven by deeper penetration in existing markets, entry into new geographies, and addition of new customers.

Establishing a greenfield cover glass and automotive display facility at Hosur, with a Phase I capital outlay of ~Rs 650 Mn (including display system assembly); equipment has been ordered and revenue contribution is expected from FY 2027-28.
PV segment future kit value guidance increased from an earlier 4-6x to now 5-8x growth from its legacy kit value.
Capacity expansion projects are underway at the Pune and Bangalore plants; expansion at Bangalore is progressing as planned.
A new facility for cover glass and display systems is coming up at Hosur; the facility is almost ready and equipment has been ordered.
The new chrome plating and painting facility at SJS Decoplast is in its final stages of commissioning.
Capacity expansion at SJS Decoplast (Pune) with an overall capex of ~Rs 1,000 Mn; the plant has been set up and is currently in its final stage of commissioning.
Capex of Rs 400-450 Mn at SJS (Bengaluru) to expand capacity and cater to a significant new business opportunity; expansion is progressing well.
PV segment kit value is guided to grow 5-8x over the legacy kit value of Rs 1,200-1,500 per vehicle, versus a current kit value of Rs 3,500-5,000 per vehicle.

SJS is increasing its focus on exploring new value-accretive acquisition opportunities as part of its inorganic growth strategy, continuing the approach that delivered SJS Decoplast (3.5x revenue growth from FY21 to FY26) and Walter Pack India (WPI).

risks.note: Heightened global conflicts, economic downturns, inflation, and supply chain disruptions present critical risks that may constrain client demand, strain end-user industries, and limit export markets, affecting the Company's growth; mitigated by generating sales from a wide customer base across multiple geographic areas and maintaining a diversified plant footprint.

The Company faces intense competition from both established and unorganised industry players; failure to consistently provide high-quality, innovative items could lead to a decline in market share and profitability. Mitigated by a strong brand identity, ability to manage over 17,500 SKUs, and a design-to-delivery model with R&D capabilities that has enabled entry into sophisticated categories with high entry barriers and few competitors.

Business and financial success may suffer from delays in day-to-day operations, poor work management, inability to meet varied customer demands, failure to deliver quality products on time, or high rejection rates; mitigated by equipment/machinery flexibility across production lines, regular process reviews, capacity planning and strict quality-control inspection.

Failure to adapt to new technological developments may affect revenue and profit margins; the Company addresses this through continuous investment in advanced technologies (e.g., the BOE Varitronix TLA for optical bonding/display systems) and a 135-member NPD team that identifies emerging trends.

Loss of key customers due to unforeseen events could negatively impact reputation and revenue growth; the risk is mitigated through market expansion and new customer acquisition, and on a consolidated basis no single customer accounts for more than 16-17% of total revenue.

Foreign exchange risk arises from the mix of importing raw materials and exporting finished goods; adverse exchange rate movements could reduce revenue or increase input costs and impact margins. Only partially managed through a natural hedge from the import/export mix, as no formal hedging arrangements were executed during the year.

Fluctuations in crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic events and high inflation, could affect margins; mitigated by long-standing supplier relationships with alternative options, negotiated price pass-through to customers after a brief delay, and Value Analysis/Value Engineering, energy conservation and waste reduction initiatives.

Shortage of skilled workers or difficulty retaining key employees could affect operations; managed through skills development, training, employee engagement programmes and an Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) to incentivise and retain high performers.
